blocks.text: 1. Global Average Pooling
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473292-294644090.png

Flattening, the previous topic, reshaped stacked feature maps into one long vector, preserving every value. Global Average Pooling is a closer look at that genuinely different alternative approach previewed in Average Pooling.
It works by averaging an entire feature map down to a single value, instead of flattening it, explored in complete depth throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview From Average Pooling
This connects back to Average Pooling's own preview of this topic, already covered in that topic. Global Average Pooling applies that same averaging idea across an entire feature map at once.
This happens rather than just a small local window, already covered throughout most of Average Pooling, extending that same summarization philosophy to its genuinely largest possible scope.
3. The Core Idea
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473292-317562704.png
Global Average Pooling's genuinely core idea takes one entire feature map, already covered in Feature Maps, as its input rather than any small local region.
It computes its genuinely single overall average, collapsing height and width entirely, leaving behind just one number that summarizes that entire feature map's own overall activation level.

blocks.text: 4. One Map, One Number
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473292-73255543.png
This connects back to one filter, one feature map, already covered in Feature Maps. Each feature map genuinely collapses down to exactly one single number under Global Average Pooling.
A layer with 512 feature maps genuinely produces a vector of exactly 512 values, one summary number per feature map, a genuinely direct, predictable relationship.
5. Global Average Pooling Versus Flattening
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473293-997780053.png
This connects back to Flattening, already covered in the previous topic. Flattening preserves genuinely every value, just reordered; Global Average Pooling instead genuinely discards most of them.

It keeps only each feature map's own genuinely single summary average, a fundamentally different tradeoff between preserving detail and genuinely compressing information, explored throughout the rest of this topic.
6. The Benefit Of Far Fewer Parameters

blocks.alt: The Benefit Of Far Fewer Parameters
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473293-102821466.png

A genuinely important, practical advantage connects back to a fully connected layer's own genuinely large parameter count, already covered in Network Architecture. Global Average Pooling's genuinely tiny output needs far fewer parameters in the layer that follows it.

This is a genuinely direct, real practical consequence of the compression already covered in the previous section, since a genuinely much smaller input vector requires genuinely far fewer connecting weights.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This parameter reduction, already covered in this topic, can be genuinely dramatic in practice, sometimes reducing a network's total parameter count by millions compared to the equivalent Flattening-based design.

blocks.text: 7. A Stronger Regularizing Effect
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473547-276542621.png

This connects back to Overfitting, already covered in its own topic. Genuinely far fewer parameters, already covered in this topic, directly reduces overfitting risk, following the same logic already covered generally for Pooling.
This gives Global Average Pooling a genuinely stronger regularizing effect than the mild one already covered for ordinary Pooling, since the parameter reduction here is genuinely far more dramatic.
8. The Strongest Translation Invariance In This Module

This connects back to translation invariance, already covered throughout the Convolution Operation and Pooling. Global Average Pooling genuinely delivers the strongest translation invariance of any technique covered in this module.

This holds since it averages across the genuinely entire feature map, position barely matters at all anymore, a genuinely extreme version of the same translation invariance benefit already covered for ordinary Pooling.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Global Average Pooling Is Genuinely The Right Choice

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Global Average Pooling Is Genuinely The Right Choice
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445473547-909616077.png

This connects back to reducing overfitting risk in genuinely large, deep networks. Its far fewer parameters, already covered in this topic, directly help with this, a genuinely valuable, practical benefit.

This connects to modern, established Convolutional Neural Network architectures, covered further in CNN Architectures. Many now genuinely prefer Global Average Pooling over Flattening as their genuinely standard default.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates applying Global Average Pooling to several stacked feature maps, contrasting the resulting vector length against Flattening's own output on the exact same input.

code.content:
import numpy as np

# Simulating 4 stacked feature maps, each 5x5, already covered in Feature Maps
rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
feature_maps = rng.normal(size=(4, 5, 5))

# Global Average Pooling, already covered as the core idea in this topic
gap_output = feature_maps.mean(axis=(1, 2))

# Flattening, already covered in the previous topic, for direct comparison
flattened_output = feature_maps.flatten()

print("Global Average Pooling output shape:", gap_output.shape, "->", gap_output)
print("Flattening output shape:", flattened_output.shape)
print(f"\nGlobal Average Pooling needs {gap_output.shape[0]} parameters per output unit in the next layer")
print(f"Flattening needs {flattened_output.shape[0]} parameters per output unit in the next layer, already covered as the parameter reduction benefit in this topic")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows Global Average Pooling producing a vector of just 4 values, one per feature map, compared to Flattening's 100 values, exactly the dramatic parameter reduction already covered in this topic.

items: Global Average Pooling averages an entire feature map down to a single value.
It extends Average Pooling's own idea to the largest possible scope: an entire feature map.
Each feature map collapses to exactly one number, unlike Flattening which preserves every value.
It needs far fewer parameters in the following layer than a Flattening-based design would.
This dramatic parameter reduction gives it a stronger regularizing effect than ordinary Pooling.
It delivers the strongest translation invariance of any technique covered in this module.
Many modern, established architectures now prefer it over Flattening as their standard default.
